ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the graph, it is known that when $x<-1$, $-2x>ax+3$. \\
Therefore, the answer is $\boxed{x<-1}$.

The inequality -2x>ax+3 means y1>y2, so look for the x-values where the y1 line lies above the y2 line. From the graph, to the left of the intersection A, the line y1=-2x is above the line y2=ax+3; to the right, it is below. Since the intersection has x-coordinate -1 and the inequality is strict, exclude x=-1. Therefore the solution set is x<-1.

method.method_draft: Use algebra after identifying the intersection. From the figure and text, A(-1,m) lies on both graphs y1=-2x and y2=ax+3. Substitute x=-1 into y1=-2x to get m=2. Since A also lies on y2=ax+3, substitute (-1,2): 2=a(-1)+3, so a=1. The inequality becomes -2x>x+3. Solving gives -3x>3, hence x<-1. Thus the solution set is x<-1.
